correctness.rationale: PASS: On E=V⊕F_p, p odd, central alternating β makes +_β a class-two exponent-p group. Direct calculation gives lambda_{(v,s)}(w,t)=(w,t+(ω−β)(v,w)), an additive automorphism; left and right brace identities hold by central bilinearity, and the Baer transform cancels β to the common additive +_0. Any multiplicative Heisenberg-group automorphism acts by a symplectic similitude P with multiplier τ and central linear shear ℓ; simultaneous preservation of +_β is equivalent to conjugacy of the ω-selfadjoint operator A_β. A selfadjoint operator over F_p[t] has symplectic hyperbolic cyclic decompositions: its invariant factors occur twice, giving diag(T,T^transpose) and one orbit for each ordinary similarity class T∈M_d(F_p). Linear shears contribute p^{2d} to the automorphism count. Rational-canonical matrix similarity enumeration yields ∏_{j>=1}(1-pu^j)^−1 and, excluding polynomial t for invertible T, ∏_{j>=1}(1-u^j)/(1-pu^j). Thus d=2 yields p²+p total, p²−1 nondegenerate/additively extraspecial. Independent enumeration of GL2(F3) conjugacy classes gave 12 total with rank split 1,3,8, consistent with bundled symplectic orbits. This classifies the stated central alternating-bilinear family only; it does not classify all skew braces or all inverse Baer deformations.

value.rationale: PASS: The fixed Heisenberg multiplication and central alternating deforming additions yield a canonical natural inverse-Baer family. Complete unmarked brace-isomorphism classes and automorphism centralizers, including the nonabelian-additive/extraspecial subfamily counts, are meaningful group-theoretic moduli data. The proof relates the brace action to classical symplectic matrix similarity and rational-canonical counting, appropriately crediting those tools. This is a family-specific exact classification, not a claim about all braces.
